title: Key Not Found: VariableSlotKey with COUNT after an alias
body:
I just upgraded from Neo4j 5.20 to 5.21 on Ubuntu. One of my queries that used to work has stopped working, using the neo4j browser, with the following error:

`Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError key not found: VariableSlotKey(b)`

Here are the steps to reproduce. Note that the error does not occur without the unique constraint.

```
CREATE (b:Banana) SET b.bananaId = 'BANANA1'
CREATE CONSTRAINT unique_bananaid FOR (b:Banana) REQUIRE b.bananaId IS UNIQUE;
MATCH (b:Banana {bananaId:'BANANA1'}) RETURN b AS banana, COUNT(b)
```

Note also that the query works if you remove the `AS banana` alias.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Thank you for the report, we will investigate this!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter thanks for reporting this. We have identified the problem and will roll out a fix in the next upcoming release. One workaround is to not not rename `b` in the query as you noted, or you can run with `CYPHER runtime=legacy...` prepended to your query, however that may affect the performance of the query somewhat.

Sorry about the problems you are facing 😞 and thanks again for bringing this to our attention!
Best regards,
Pontus

That has caused other issues as the CypherDSL library creates queries that don't work with legacy mode. 

Are there anymore options?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I have encountered this same bug first with 5.22.0 community on Linux, and also with 5.23.0 community.

Here is a generic version of the query which produced the error:

```
MATCH (a:A {id:'xx'})
MATCH (a) -[r1]-> (b:B)
WHERE a.value = false OR a.value IS NULL
WITH a,b

OPTIONAL MATCH (a2:A) -[r2]-> (c:C) -[r3]-> (b)
WITH a, b, a2

RETURN a, b, COLLECT(a2.id) AS ids
```

Observations:
* running the query as above results in this error: `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError key not found: VariableSlotKey(a)`
* changing the RETURN statement to `RETURN a, b, a2` (can do `a2.id`, too) runs without error – it's not the query result I want, but it shows that the labels involved are valid, etc.
* running the query against other data sets (test database) works fine – the query itself behaves differently based on the data
* adding "CYPHER runtime=legacy" to start of the query changed the behavior, but it's still an error:
   ```
   Neo.DatabaseError.Statement.ExecutionFailed Unknown variable `a`.
   ```
* the error is present both in code (using Neo4j Java driver) and the browser-based query tool

@participant2 thanks for the reply. I addressed your questions below. Please let me know if I can provide any further information.

> @participant5 Just to clarify you are not seeing failure for the query that was initially poster in this issue right? You are referring to

> MATCH (a:A {id:'xx'})
> MATCH (a) -[r1]-> (b:B)

Correct, I'm seeing the error with the query posted above.

> I am trying to reproduce the error you are seeing but so far I haven't been able to. Could you share how you have set up the database before running the query?

This occurs with a basic database setup (no changes to `neo4j.conf`). 

The following is run once at application startup, so it is reused by all callers:
```
protected static final Driver driver = GraphDatabase.driver(uri, AuthTokens.basic(user, password));
```

All queries are run in a transaction, where each caller gets a transaction (like below) and is responsible for calling `commit()` or `rollback()` appropriately:
```
import org.neo4j.driver.Session;
import org.neo4j.driver.Transaction;
import org.neo4j.driver.TransactionConfig;

public static Transaction beginTransaction(int timeoutInSeconds) {
    Session session = driver.session();
    TransactionConfig config = TransactionConfig.builder()
            .withTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(timeoutInSeconds))
            .build();
    return session.beginTransaction(config);
}
```

> Can you share the plan? (run the query with `EXPLAIN` prepended and click the `Export TXT` and just paste it here if you are using Browser).

Running the query (through the web browser) with `EXPLAIN` does not return a query plan, only the same error (like below). I am familiar with how to show a query plan, but this particular query does not generate one (only an error).
```
Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError
key not found: VariableSlotKey(user)
```

Also, this behavior remains using Neo4j Community 5.25.1.
